title: Questel Orbit overview: Features, pricing, and alternatives
summary: Questel Orbit overview of patent search, Sophia AI, pricing, security, and buyer fit, with alternatives for litigation, portfolio, and R&D teams.
body_markdown:
Questel Orbit Intelligence combines professional patent search, family-level records, and portfolio analysis in one platform. Buyers also need to understand where Sophia artificial intelligence (AI) fits, which modules sit outside the base subscription, and how far the workflow extends past a relevant hit. We focus on practical fit for search, analytics, and patent litigation.


**Review scope:** &AI publishes this guide and is one of the alternatives discussed. This overview draws on Questel’s public product materials and knowledge base, with key product, security, and pricing sources checked on October 5, 2026. We did not test a live subscriber account, so this is not a hands-on assessment of search quality or usability.


## Key takeaways


- **Orbit is a serious option for expert patent search and high-volume family analytics.** Its query controls, FAMPAT family structure, alerts, workfiles, and analysis tools fit recurring search, monitoring, portfolio, and landscape work.
- **Sophia now does more than semantic ranking.** Features Mode returns paragraph- and claim-linked snippets and an Excel prior art report. Sophia Document supports source-linked patent review, and the multi-document workflow compares families. Access, caps, and credits vary by subscription.
- **Questel uses a quote-led sales model.** Its public Orbit page shows “Request a demo” and no list price. That does not establish that trials, institutional access, or another no-cost route are unavailable.
- **We recommend our platform when litigation work product is the endpoint.** Our Prior Art Search covers patents, non-patent literature (NPL), and products, while our litigation workspace carries selected evidence into invalidity, infringement, claim-chart, and drafting workflows.


## Questel Orbit login, support, and training


Questel’s current[login directory](https://www.questel.com/login-page/) places the product under **Orbit – Patent Intelligence Software** . Choose **Intelligence** , which routes to the[Orbit Intelligence login](https://intelligence.orbit.com/) . Do not choose Insight or Express unless that is the product your organization licensed.


Use these official destinations for account and product help:


- [Orbit single sign-on](https://login.orbit.com/) for organizations configured for single sign-on (SSO)
- [Orbit knowledge base](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/home) for current feature and workflow documentation
- [Questel product training](https://www.questel.com/trainings/) for public training listings, including free online customer sessions and paid expert training


## Questel Orbit fit based on public materials


Based on Questel’s public product and support materials, Orbit fits teams that repeatedly search global patent data, normalize families, monitor new records, and analyze large portfolios. Questel’s[current product page](https://www.questel.com/patent/ip-intelligence-software/orbit-intelligence/) describes more than 100 million patents, 17 million designs, and 150 million NPL records, plus ownership, legal-status, citation, litigation, opposition, licensing, and standard-essential-patent data.


The product’s value is clearest when the unit of work is a family, patent procedure, search set, alert, or portfolio. It can support prior art and validity research, and its current Sophia features add useful disclosure-level review. A similarity label or AI-extracted feature still requires expert verification against the original document. Questel says this directly in its Sophia documentation.


For litigation, the distinction is the endpoint. Orbit helps a team find, review, and analyze patent records at scale. Our workspace also performs portfolio search and litigation-focused portfolio analysis, with a different center of gravity: litigation analysis, limitation mapping, product evidence, charts, contention drafts subject to attorney review, and editable work product.


## What is Orbit Intelligence?


Orbit Intelligence is the expert search and analytics product within Questel’s broader[IP intelligence software](https://www.questel.com/patent/ip-intelligence-software/) portfolio. The product names and modules should be separated before comparing a quote.


Offering How Questel currently presents it Buying implication


**Orbit Intelligence** Patent searching and analysis platform Confirm the license level, users, collections, exports, alerts, workfiles, and analysis functions in the quote


**AI-Classifier, Prosecution Pack, and Chemistry** Special modules associated with Orbit Intelligence Treat each as separately scoped until the order form says it is included


**Orbit BioSequence, Orbit Insight, Orbit Express, and Orbit Intellixir** Related IP intelligence products A capability shown in one product should not be assumed to exist in Orbit Intelligence


**Sophia** Cross-platform AI capabilities available inside products including Orbit Intelligence Access differs by feature and by Essential, Advanced, or Premium license


**SEP Database** A separately marketed standard-essential patent (SEP) solution Basic SEP identification exists in the standard patent collections; the[dedicated SEP search](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000574470-introducing-sep-paid-module-definitions-search-and-analysis) is a paid module that an Orbit administrator activates for licensed users


Questel publicly states that Orbit can analyze up to **2 million records in a live analysis** and save analyses of up to **30,000 records** . Those caps appear on the[Orbit product page](https://www.questel.com/patent/ip-intelligence-software/orbit-intelligence/) without an Essential, Advanced, or Premium attribution, so a buyer should not assign them to a tier unless the quote does so.


## How Questel Orbit search works


Orbit offers several routes into the same patent data. Easy Search recognizes keywords, names, classifications, and patent numbers. Advanced Search adds fields, dates, classifications, assignees, legal status, templates, and command-line control. Sophia Query converts a natural-language request into an editable Boolean query. Sophia Search uses embeddings for semantic retrieval and can add feature-level disclosure analysis.


### Start with the right collection


The[collection guide](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000437207) defines three different records:


Collection One result represents Good fit Important limit


**FAMPAT** One invention-based family Global prior art review, portfolio search, landscapes, competitor monitoring, and deduplicated screening Terms can occur in different family members; inspect the publication stage that supplies the relied-on disclosure


**FULLPAT** One application or national procedure with its publication stages Jurisdiction-focused work, freedom-to-operate (FTO) review, and procedure-level analysis The same invention can appear in several country records;[FULLPAT records cannot be saved to workfiles](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000437372-coverage-of-the-fullpat-database)


**FULLTEXT** One published full-text document Publication-stage searches and fast intake of office data Records without full text are absent, publication stages create duplicates, and the Analysis module is unavailable


FAMPAT is the default. Questel calls it a **strict enriched family** . The strict starting rule groups members that share the same priority numbers. Enrichment rules account for procedures such as Patent Cooperation Treaty and European national phases, European divisionals, and certain office-specific cases. Families are dynamic as new data arrives, and a publication appears in only one FAMPAT family. The[FAMPAT construction rules](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000436698) also acknowledge that incorrect source priority or application data can produce grouping errors.


That structure reduces duplicate review. It does not decide whether an individual publication qualifies as prior art or carries the date a litigation position requires.


### Easy Search and command-line search serve different jobs


[Easy Search](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000436704-easy-search) is a field-routing assistant, rather than a semantic search box. A keyword is searched first in the` /BI` and` /SA` text fields, then in assignee and inventor fields, and may expand to full text when results are sparse. Classification codes go to International Patent Classification and Cooperative Patent Classification fields. Recognized numbers go to publication, application, and priority-number fields.


Advanced and command-line search provide the precision experienced searchers expect. The main[Orbit operators](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000437870) have specific behavior:


Syntax Function Practical caution


` AND` ,` OR` ,` NOT` Boolean combination or exclusion In FAMPAT,` AND` terms can occur in different family members;` NOT` can remove a relevant long document


` F` Terms in the same field, across publications in a record It is broader than same-paragraph or same-sentence searching


` P` Terms in the same paragraph, up to 100 sentences Behavior depends on the structure supplied by the patent office


` S` Terms in the same sentence, up to 200 terms Sentence boundaries depend on source text


` nD` Terms separated by no more than *n* words, either order, in the same sentence Chained distances inside parentheses can add together


` nW` Terms separated by no more than *n* words, in the entered order, in the same sentence Chained distances can add together here too


` +` ,` ?` ,` #` Any number, zero or one, or exactly one replacement character A truncated stem needs at least three characters; short stems create noise


` _` Joined, hyphenated, or space-separated forms It is an operator, rather than a truncation symbol


The command line supports careful, reproducible iteration. Searchers still need to inspect term expansion, family-member matches, translations, and exclusions before treating recall or precision as settled.


## What Sophia AI currently adds


Sophia is now a set of distinct functions. Grouping them under one “AI search” label obscures meaningful differences.


Function Current behavior Publicly documented access and caps


**[Sophia Query](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000574749)** Converts a natural-language request into a focused, editable English Boolean query with proposed synonyms, classifications, authorities, names, and dates Questel cautions that its goal is focus, rather than exhaustiveness


**[Sophia Search, Semantic Mode](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000587553-sophia-search-ai-powered-semantic-search)** Ranks FAMPAT families using embeddings generated from the input and a computational family member Questel documents this mode as available without usage limits; it uses the first 3,000 input characters


**Sophia Search, Features Mode** Extracts up to 10 technical features, ranks results by feature coverage, and supplies up to three paragraph- or claim-linked snippets per disclosed feature Advanced gets 20 monthly credits and Premium gets 40; Essential gets no Features Mode credits; one completed Features Mode search consumes one credit


**Sophia Document** Chats with one selected patent family member, links answers to paragraph and claim numbers, and offers technical, claims, and data-extraction prompts Advanced and Premium only; Expert responses use one credit from monthly allocations of 100 and 200 respectively; the Fast model is free; unavailable in workfiles


**Sophia Multi-Document** Corpus and parallel review across selected families, with patent, paragraph, or claim references Uses the representative member and shares Sophia Document credits; both Expert and Fast models consume credits in different proportions. Review is limited to the current hit-list page and the context window; Questel describes batches of 20, 50, or 100 families depending on scope


Features Mode is materially more useful than a bare similarity score. The[current Features Mode documentation](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000585238-sophia-search-ai-powered-text-analysis-disclosure-reveal) shows disclosure statuses, supporting snippets, and an XLS export. For up to 10 selected results, Orbit can generate an Excel prior art report with search information, a feature table showing possible disclosure across publication stages, and a document table with titles, abstracts, and permalinks.


[Sophia Document](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000583978) adds source links to its answers. The[multi-document workflow](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000597845-sophia-document-with-multi-documents) can synthesize a corpus or run the same prompt across families. Both workflows can shorten initial review. Questel instructs users to verify responses with their own expertise and the original patent text, notes that long documents can exceed model context, and identifies nondeterministic output as a limitation.


## How Questel describes security and AI data handling


Questel publishes three kinds of security and data-handling statements: Orbit-specific AI technology and provider terms, broader company AI commitments, and a general personal-data policy. They apply at different levels and should not be read as one universal retention or hosting promise.


The Orbit-specific[AI tools usage disclaimer](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000582693) places Sophia Query, Sophia Search text analysis and disclosure, Sophia Document, Sophia Lab, and most other AI features, including claims explanations, in an OpenAI setup on dedicated Questel servers hosted in Microsoft Azure, with inference localized in Europe. For that setup, Questel states that there is no data retention, no training or reuse, no human-based abuse monitoring, and no sharing of personal information with third parties.


The same disclaimer separately identifies a locally installed AI model for Sophia Query audio-to-text transcription and a locally installed specialized large language model for Sophia Search semantic search and embedding creation. It says customers in mainland China use Alibaba’s Qwen models through Alibaba’s application programming interface. Questel notes that its list of technologies and providers may change.


The Orbit disclaimer’s no-retention statement is specific to the identified OpenAI setup. It does not mean every Orbit record disappears after inference. The[Sophia Search data-handling details](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000585238-sophia-search-ai-powered-text-analysis-disclosure-reveal) say uploaded source documents remain on Orbit servers for AI processing and are discarded when the search reaches the hit list, while the search history stores the input text, prefilters, features, and related settings. The[Sophia Document guidance](https://intelligence.help.questel.com/en/support/solutions/articles/77000583978) says a patent chat remains in the user’s personal Orbit data until the user selects Reset Chat, and that the chat is private to that user.


Questel’s separate[Trusted AI commitments](https://www.questel.com/questel-trusted-ai/) set broader company-level terms. Questel says information supplied for AI inference is not used to train or fine-tune models and is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or later. It limits access to business data stored on its systems to authorized employees who need it for engineering support, investigating possible platform abuse, or legal compliance, and to specialized third-party contractors bound by confidentiality and security obligations solely to review abuse and misuse. The page also says deleted conversations are removed within 30 days unless Questel must retain them by law. These company-level commitments are distinct from the Orbit-specific provider and feature terms above.


Questel’s group[AI policy](https://www.questel.com/questels-artificial-intelligence-policy/) describes the company as ISO 27001 certified and refers to access control, encryption, continuous monitoring, regular audits, and a contractual framework using a master services agreement, data processing agreement, and Standard Contractual Clauses. The public policy does not identify the certificate number, certification scope, or an Orbit-specific certification boundary. Questel’s[general privacy policy](https://www.questel.com/questel-data-privacy-policy/) covers its websites, software-as-a-service platforms, and offline business relationships. It says personal data is retained for as long as needed for the relevant purpose and legal, accounting, reporting, or dispute obligations, and that international transfers may use Standard Contractual Clauses. It does not set one retention period for all Orbit data.


## Where Orbit’s output differs from litigation analysis


A candidate reference needs legal qualification and limitation-level analysis before it supports an invalidity position. Patent legal status, family similarity, and an AI disclosure label answer different questions.


### Qualify the reference under the applicable version of Section 102


The Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (AIA) transition rule generally brings the current statute into play for patents or applications that contain or contained a claim with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, with additional rules for certain priority references. Patents outside that transition rule can remain under pre-AIA law. The[AIA transition provision](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-112publ29/pdf/PLAW-112publ29.pdf) and the patent’s prosecution record control the determination.


Under current[35 U.S.C. § 102](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/mpep-9015-appx-l.html#al_d1fbe1_234ed_52) :


- Section 102(a)(1) looks to patents, printed publications, public use, on-sale activity, and other public availability before the claimed invention’s effective filing date, subject to the exceptions in Section 102(b)(1).
- Section 102(a)(2) covers certain U.S. patents and published applications naming another inventor that were effectively filed before the claimed invention’s effective filing date, subject to Section 102(b)(2).
- Section 102(d) can carry an application or patent back to an earlier priority or benefit date only for subject matter described in the earlier application. The Federal Circuit’s August 2026 decision in[Dental Monitoring v. Align](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/25-1752.OPINION.8-10-2026_2736022.pdf) confirms that reliance on an earlier provisional date requires Section 112(a) support.


Pre-AIA[Section 102](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/mpep-9015-appx-l.html#d0e302383) uses different subsections, dates, and exceptions, including the former one-year statutory bar. A publication date, filing date, priority claim, and public-access date should therefore be recorded separately.


For NPL and product materials, capture evidence of when the relied-on content became publicly accessible. The Federal Circuit treats public accessibility as the touchstone for a printed publication, and a page’s mere existence on the web may be insufficient.[Blue Calypso v. Groupon](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/15-1391.opinion.2-29-2016.1.pdf) illustrates the fact-specific inquiry. Patent expiration, lapse, or abandonment does not by itself answer whether the disclosure qualifies as prior art.


### Map anticipation, obviousness, and Section 112 separately


For anticipation under Section 102, a single enabling reference must disclose every limitation expressly or inherently, with the elements arranged or combined as claimed. The Federal Circuit applies the disclosure and arrangement rule in[Blue Calypso](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/15-1391.opinion.2-29-2016.1.pdf) , relying on *Net MoneyIN v. VeriSign* and the court’s inherency cases.[MPEP § 2121](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/s2121.html) summarizes the enablement requirement and supporting cases.


For obviousness,[35 U.S.C. § 103](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/mpep-9015-appx-l.html#al_d1fbe1_19797_b0) asks whether the differences between the claimed invention and prior art would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill before the effective filing date.[Graham v. John Deere](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-383/USREPORTS-383-1/context) supplies the factual framework, and[KSR v. Teleflex](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-550/USREPORTS-550-398/context) requires a flexible analysis of the reason a skilled person would combine or modify the art.


Section 112 defenses remain separate. Written description, enablement, and definiteness concern the challenged patent’s specification and claims under[35 U.S.C. § 112](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/mpep-9015-appx-l.html#d0e302824912) . They should not be blended into a Section 102 or 103 coverage table.


In district court, each patent claim carries the[Section 282 presumption of validity](https://www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/mpep-9015-appx-l.html#d0e305845) . The challenger bears the burden, and[Microsoft v. i4i](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-564/pdf/USREPORTS-564-91.pdf) holds that invalidity must be proved by clear and convincing evidence. Art that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office did not consider can affect the evidentiary weight without lowering that standard.


## Questel Orbit alternatives by buyer job


Orbit alternatives make sense only after the buyer fixes the job and final deliverable. A database replacement, an R&D intelligence platform, and a litigation workspace solve different parts of the process.


Clarivate’s current name for Derwent Innovation is **[Derwent Patent Search (formerly Derwent Innovation)](https://clarivate.com/intellectual-property/derwent/patent-search/)** .


Product Buyer job it fits Center of the workflow Output to evaluate in a pilot


**[&AI](https://www.tryandai.com/product)** Patent litigation, invalidity, infringement detection, litigation-focused portfolio review Search across patents, NPL, and product materials, followed by source-linked legal analysis and drafting Limitation mappings, evidence-of-use and invalidity charts, Section 102 and 103 analysis, Section 112[written-description analysis](https://www.tryandai.com/product/invalidity-analysis) ,[contention drafts subject to attorney review](https://www.tryandai.com/product/invalidity-analysis) , and editable exports


**Derwent Patent Search (formerly Derwent Innovation)** Professional patent search where human-authored invention summaries and curated family data matter Patent and NPL retrieval, Derwent World Patents Index summaries, citation review, and search analytics Recall on a known search, family handling, summary quality, and downstream export usability


**[Patsnap](https://www.patsnap.com/products/analytics/)** Research and development (R&D), technology scouting, competitive intelligence, and innovation strategy Patent, science, technology, litigation, and market data connected for research and portfolio decisions Landscape quality, competitor and technology monitoring, scientific context, and team reporting


For buyers comparing these with Orbit, we would keep Orbit in the test as the family-analytics baseline. Derwent Patent Search is the closer alternative for a trained patent search group. Patsnap is the closer alternative for an R&D or innovation team. Shortlist &AI when the project begins with patent, NPL, product, or portfolio research and must end in reviewable litigation work product.

## Questel Orbit pricing and packaging


As of October 5, 2026, Questel’s Orbit Intelligence page offers[Request a demo](https://www.questel.com/patent/ip-intelligence-software/orbit-intelligence/) and does not display a public list price. The knowledge base nevertheless documents Essential, Advanced, and Premium licenses, feature-specific monthly credits, optional modules, and a paid dedicated SEP module. The working configuration matters more than a single seat quote.


Ask Questel to state these items in the order form:


1. License level, user count, and access for each user type
2. Included collections, analysis, alerts, workfiles, exports, and presentation functions
3. Sophia Query, Semantic Mode, Features Mode, Document, and Multi-Document access
4. Monthly Sophia credits, refill rules, and any overage path
5. AI-Classifier, Prosecution Pack, Chemistry, and other special modules
6. General SEP fields versus the dedicated paid SEP module
7. The 2-million live-analysis and 30,000 saved-analysis caps, plus contractual workfile and export limits
8. Training, support, implementation, SSO, application programming interface access, and renewal terms
9. AI provider routing by region, input and chat retention, deletion timing, model-training restrictions, encryption, the data processing agreement, and the current ISO 27001 certificate scope


For comparison, our[public pricing](https://www.tryandai.com/pricing) as of October 5, 2026 lists Pay as You Go at **$0.40 per credit** with no monthly commitment, Pro at **$625 per user per month** with 2,500 credits and $0.25 additional credits, and custom Enterprise pricing. All plans include the same core platform access, and we offer a 7-day free trial.


## A practical buyer pilot


Use a completed search or known matter instead of a vendor-curated example. The pilot should test the handoff from query to the deliverable your team actually needs.


1. **Choose a known target and a hard negative.** The target tests retrieval. The hard negative shows how much review noise a similarity or feature score introduces.
2. **Run FAMPAT and FULLPAT.** Compare family construction, member selection, jurisdiction handling, publication stages, priority data, and legal-status treatment.
3. **Use three search paths.** Build one advanced Boolean query, one Sophia Query, and one Sophia Search. Record which terms, classifications, filters, and family members drive each result.
4. **Verify five candidates at source.** Capture the relied-on publication and passage, applicable AIA or pre-AIA rule, effective filing and publication dates, priority support, and evidence of public accessibility. Track legal status separately for FTO or portfolio questions.
5. **Complete the real output.** Finish a landscape, portfolio report, invalidity chart, evidence-of-use chart, or memo. Measure the manual steps after the relevant hit appears.
6. **Price the working configuration.** Include the correct license tier, Sophia credits, modules, training, exports, and renewal terms.


Orbit deserves a place in pilots centered on expert patent search and family analytics. If your pilot ends with limitation-level litigation analysis, product evidence, charts, and drafts,[start your 7-day free trial](https://platform.tryandai.com/sign-up) and run the same matter in our workspace.
